rationale: A wins because it keeps four clean beats separate and refuses the shiny hallucination instead of pitching around it. Its best line, "A grocery marketplace built a $1B ad business out of 6,000 brands," is a real retail-media trade story with proof requirements attached. B has useful work, but "The carts that skip checkout could be feeding the ad engine that just crossed $1 billion" promotes an unconfirmed data link into an angle; the caveat is honest, but the slot is still doing speculation's laundry.
gaps_in_A: "Instacart's delivery growth has stalled" overstates the supplied fact. The update says order growth slowed to single digits; slow growth is not the same as stalled growth.

"Why 1,500 grocery banners are renting their tech stack instead of building it" leans harder than the facts allow. The update says Instacart partners with 1,500+ banners, not that all are renting carts, ads, or a full tech stack.
"The checkout line is quietly disappearing from a few hundred grocery stores" is a little too neat. Caper carts can skip checkout, but the facts do not say checkout lines are disappearing storewide.

The set could ask more directly whether smart carts, ads, and delivery are separate businesses or one data loop. It rightly refuses the unproven ad-surface claim, but the strategic question still needs a clean version.
gaps_in_B: "The carts that skip checkout could be feeding the ad engine that just crossed $1 billion" is the dangerous one. The set admits nothing confirms the link, then spends a full angle on it anyway.

"More grocery chains are letting Instacart's smart carts run their checkout line" and "Instacart's smart-cart rollout turns it into checkout infrastructure for grocery chains" overlap too much. One is store operations, one is vendor strategy, but they are still standing on the same square of floor.
"computer-vision retail" is not in the supplied facts. AI-powered carts may use computer vision, but the update does not say that; a reporter will not grade on vibes.
It misses the cleanest ad-trade angle: $1B annual run rate plus 6,000 consumer brands buying ads. Instead it jumps from retail media to privacy speculation before exhausting the grounded story.
